title: Paperwork: Skatteverket, contracts and official letters
title_target: Ett mejl räcker, förutsatt att jag svarar och bekräftar det.
goal: Handle Swedish bureaucracy with confidence: register an address, ask the right questions at a counter, understand a sublet contract and decode an official letter.
bekal: you can explain your business at a government office and ask what something means
you can discuss notice, deposit and permission in a second-hand rental contract
you can read an official letter and translate officialese into everyday Swedish
wave: Go back to Unit 17 (Compound words): split *flyttanmälan*, *förstahandskontrakt*, *uppsägningstid*, *hyresvärd* and *arbetsgivare* into their parts, then say each one aloud with the stress on the first part.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — På servicekontoret
dialogs.intro: Dian has lived in Majorna since August, but a letter from her bank has just been returned to the sender: she never registered her new address. She goes to the government service office in the city center, and a case officer calls her number.

lines.speaker: Handläggaren:
lines.text: Hej och välkommen. Vad gäller det?
lines.id: Hello and welcome. What can I help you with?
lines.literal: hi and welcome. what concerns it?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hej. Jag bor i Göteborg sedan augusti, men jag har aldrig anmält min nya adress.
lines.id: Hi. I've been living in Göteborg since August, but I've never registered my new address.
lines.literal: hi. I live in Göteborg since August, but I have never reported my new address.

lines.speaker: Handläggaren:
lines.text: Det borde du ha gjort inom en vecka. Men bättre sent än aldrig. Har du personnummer?
lines.id: You should have done that within a week. But better late than never. Do you have a personal identity number?
lines.literal: that should you have done within a week. but better late than never. have you personal-number?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ja, jag fick det när jag bodde i Stockholm. Men jag hyr i andra hand, så det står någon annans namn på dörren.
lines.id: Yes, I got it when I lived in Stockholm. But I'm subletting, so there's someone else's name on the door.
lines.literal: yes, I got it when I lived in Stockholm. but I rent in second hand, so it stands someone else's name on door-the.

lines.speaker: Handläggaren:
lines.text: Inga problem. I flyttanmälan skriver du c/o och namnet på den som har förstahandskontraktet.
lines.id: No problem. In the change-of-address notice you write c/o and the name of the person who holds the main lease.
lines.literal: no problems. in move-notification-the write you c/o and name-the on the-one who has first-hand-contract-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Okej. Och hur lång tid tar det innan adressen är registrerad?
lines.id: OK. And how long does it take before the address is registered?
lines.literal: okay. and how long time takes it before address-the is registered?

lines.speaker: Handläggaren:
lines.text: Oftast en till två veckor. Du får ett brev hem när ändringen är gjord.
lines.id: Usually one to two weeks. You'll get a letter at home when the change has been made.
lines.literal: most-often one to two weeks. you get a letter home when change-the is done.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Bra. En sak till: jag får lön för min praktik. Hur fungerar det med skatten?
lines.id: Good. One more thing: I'm paid for my internship. How does the tax work?
lines.literal: good. one thing more: I get salary for my internship. how works it with tax-the?

lines.speaker: Handläggaren:
lines.text: Arbetsgivaren drar av skatten innan lönen betalas ut. Sedan deklarerar du i vår.
lines.id: Your employer deducts the tax before the salary is paid out. Then you file a tax return this spring.
lines.literal: work-giver-the draws off tax-the before salary-the is-paid out. then declare you in spring.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Deklarerar? Måste jag fylla i massor av blanketter?
lines.id: File a tax return? Do I have to fill in loads of forms?
lines.literal: declare? must I fill in masses of forms?

lines.speaker: Handläggaren:
lines.text: Nej, för de flesta räcker det att godkänna deklarationen digitalt med BankID.
lines.id: No, for most people it's enough to approve the tax return digitally with BankID.
lines.literal: no, for the most suffices it to approve declaration-the digitally with BankID.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det låter nästan för enkelt för att vara sant.
lines.id: That sounds almost too easy to be true.
lines.literal: that sounds almost too simple for to be true.

lines.speaker: Handläggaren:
lines.text: Sverige är bra på blanketter, men ännu bättre på appar.
lines.id: Sweden is good at forms, but even better at apps.
lines.literal: Sweden is good on forms, but even better on apps.

notes: **Vad gäller det?** — literally "What does it concern?": the standard opening at any counter or on the phone to an authority. Answer with the same verb: *Det gäller min adress* (It's about my address). Say **vah YEL-ler deh**.

**Det borde du ha gjort inom en vecka** — modal + perfect from Unit 5, and a real rule: a move must be reported to Skatteverket within one week. The notice itself is *en flyttanmälan*: *flytt* (move) + *anmälan* (notification), a compound of the kind you took apart in Unit 17. *Anmäla* means to report or register something officially: *anmäla en adress*, *anmäla ett brott* (report a crime), *anmäla sig till en kurs* (sign up for a course).

**Hyra i andra hand** — "to rent in second hand": to sublet from the person who holds the actual lease, the *förstahandskontrakt*. In Göteborg and Stockholm the queue for a first-hand rental can be ten years or more, so subletting is how most newcomers start. You will also see it written as one word: *andrahandsuthyrning*, *ett andrahandskontrakt*.
**c/o** — exactly as in English, "care of", and Swedes even say it in English: **kehr ov**. Without it on your letterbox and in the register, your post may never reach you.

**Drar av skatten** — *dra av* (particle verb, stress on *AV*) means to deduct. Notice the s-passive in *innan lönen betalas ut* (before the salary is paid out), the typical style of official explanations you practiced in Unit 13.

**Deklarera** — to file your income tax return. Every spring Skatteverket sends a pre-filled return; most people check it and approve it in the app with **BankID**, the electronic ID that Swedes use for banking, healthcare, signing contracts and almost everything else.

grammars.title: At the counter: getting the information you need
body: Officials in Sweden are generally helpful, but they answer the question you ask. These phrases help you ask the right one, and check that you have understood.

head: You want to…
Svenska
rows: Det gäller min adress. / Jag skulle vilja anmäla…
Vilka handlingar behöver jag ta med?
Kan du ta det lite långsammare?

after: **Innebära** (to mean, to involve) is the word for what a rule or a decision means in practice; **betyda** is for what a word means. *Vad betyder ”deklaration”?* asks for a translation; *Vad innebär det för mig?* asks what you will actually have to do.
*Handläggningstiden* is the processing time and *en handläggare* is the case officer: the person who handles (*handlägger*) your case.

grammars.title: Official words and everyday words
body: Swedish authorities have worked hard since the 1970s to write plain Swedish (*klarspråk*), and since 2009 the Language Act requires their language to be "cultivated, simple and comprehensible". Even so, letters and forms still contain a layer of formal words. Learn to recognize them, but use the everyday words yourself.
after: **Dock** is an adverb, not a conjunction: it sits in the middle of the clause like *inte*. *Ansökan kom dock in för sent* (The application, however, arrived too late).

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Andrahandskontraktet
dialogs.intro: January. Dian's internship ends in February, and she may move back to Stockholm. She video-calls Hanna in Berlin, with their sublet contract open on the kitchen table.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hej Hanna! Har du tid en kvart? Jag har kontraktet framför mig.
lines.id: Hi Hanna! Have you got fifteen minutes? I've got the contract in front of me.
lines.literal: hi Hanna! have you time a quarter? I have contract-the in-front-of me.

lines.speaker: Hanna:
lines.text: Absolut. Är det något som är oklart?
lines.id: Absolutely. Is anything unclear?
lines.literal: absolutely. is it something that is unclear?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Praktiken slutar i februari, och jag flyttar kanske tillbaka till Stockholm. Vad står det om uppsägningstid?
lines.id: The internship ends in February, and I may move back to Stockholm. What does it say about the notice period?
lines.literal: internship-the ends in February, and I move maybe back to Stockholm. what stands it about notice-time?

lines.speaker: Hanna:
lines.text: Att vi båda har en månads uppsägningstid. Om du vill flytta i slutet av februari säger du upp kontraktet senast den sista januari.
lines.id: That we both have one month's notice. If you want to move out at the end of February, you give notice by January 31 at the latest.
lines.literal: that we both have a month's notice-time. if you want move in end-the of February say you up contract-the latest the last January.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Och måste uppsägningen vara skriftlig?
lines.id: And does the notice have to be in writing?
lines.literal: and must notice-the be written?

lines.speaker: Hanna:
lines.text: Ja, enligt kontraktet. Ett mejl räcker, förutsatt att jag svarar och bekräftar det.
lines.id: Yes, according to the contract. An email is enough, provided that I reply and confirm it.
lines.literal: yes, according-to contract-the. an email suffices, presupposed that I answer and confirm it.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Bra. Och depositionen, får jag tillbaka hela?
lines.id: Good. And the deposit, do I get all of it back?
lines.literal: good. and deposit-the, get I back whole?

lines.speaker: Hanna:
lines.text: Hela beloppet, såvida inget har gått sönder. Och att badrummet var avstängt i höstas räknas inte!
lines.id: The full amount, as long as nothing has been broken. And the bathroom being closed last fall doesn't count!
lines.literal: whole amount-the, provided nothing has gone asunder. and that bathroom-the was shut-off in autumn doesn't count!

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Tur det. Men om jag får stanna i Göteborg? Kan vi förlänga i så fall?
lines.id: Lucky me. But what if I get to stay in Göteborg? Could we extend in that case?
lines.literal: luck that. but if I get stay in Göteborg? can we lengthen in so case?

lines.speaker: Hanna:
lines.text: Det beror på hyresvärden. Mitt tillstånd att hyra ut gäller bara till sista juni.
lines.id: That depends on the landlord. My permission to sublet is only valid until the end of June.
lines.literal: it depends on rent-host-the. my permission to rent out applies only to last June.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Och efter det? Kan du inte bara fortsätta hyra ut?
lines.id: And after that? Can't you just carry on subletting?
lines.literal: and after that? can you not just continue rent out?

lines.speaker: Hanna:
lines.text: Nej, inte utan nytt tillstånd. Annars kan jag bli av med lägenheten, och du med.
lines.id: No, not without new permission. Otherwise I could lose the apartment, and so could you.
lines.literal: no, not without new permission. otherwise can I become off with apartment-the, and you with.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Då vet jag. Jag hör av mig så fort jag vet mer om jobbet.
lines.id: Then I know where I stand. I'll be in touch as soon as I know more about the job.
lines.literal: then know I. I hear from me so fast I know more about job-the.

notes: **Har du tid en kvart?** — *en kvart* (a quarter of an hour) is how Swedes ask for "a few minutes" that are actually meant: *om en kvart* (in fifteen minutes). **Oklart** (unclear) shows the prefix *o-*, Swedish *un-*: *oklar, ovanlig, olycklig*.

**Säger du upp kontraktet** — *säga upp* (stress on *UPP*) means to terminate a contract or to resign from a job; *säga till* (stress on *TILL*) just means to let someone know. *Uppsägningstid* (notice period) comes from the first: **ÜP-sehg-nings-teed**. *Senast den sista januari* = by January 31 at the latest.

**Skriftlig, enligt kontraktet** — *skriftlig* (in writing) is the opposite of *muntlig* (spoken, oral). Under Swedish rental law, notice must be given in writing, and an agreement "by phone" is hard to prove later. *Enligt* (according to) is one of the most frequent words in official Swedish.

**Förutsatt att, såvida** — two conditions that are typical of contracts: *förutsatt att* (provided that) and *såvida* (as long as; with *inte*, unless). See the grammar box. *Hela beloppet* is "the full amount": *ett belopp* is the formal word for a sum of money.

**Tillstånd att hyra ut** — for a normal rental apartment, the first-hand tenant needs the landlord's permission to sublet, and it is always for a limited period. Without it, the tenant can lose the lease, and the subtenant can lose their home at very short notice. Asking to see the permission is not rude in Sweden; it is smart.

**Bli av med … och du med** — *bli av med* means to lose or to get rid of: *bli av med lägenheten*, *bli av med jobbet*, *Äntligen blev jag av med förkylningen!* In speech, *med* at the end also means "too": *och du med* = and you too. **Jag hör av mig** = I'll be in touch.

grammars.title: Conditions in contracts and rules
body: Contracts and official texts are full of conditions. Beyond *om* (if), these are the connectors you will meet. All of them except the last two start a subordinate clause, so BIFF applies: *såvida du **inte** säger upp kontraktet*.

head: Svenska
English
Example
rows: Om du vill flytta, säg till i god tid.
Spara kvittot ifall något går sönder.
Du får ha katt förutsatt att du städar efter den.
Du får tillbaka pengarna så länge inget är trasigt.
Kontraktet gäller ett år, såvida det inte sägs upp.
Fråga om tillstånd, annars kan du bli av med bostaden.
Är hyran för hög? I så fall kan du kontakta hyresnämnden.

after: **Annars** and **i så fall** are adverbs, not subordinating words. When they open a clause, the verb comes straight after them (V2): *annars **kan** du…*, *i så fall **kan** du…*.
*Hyresnämnden* (the Rent Tribunal) is where tenants can turn if the rent is unreasonable, including second-hand rent.

blocks.text: Two weeks after Dian's visit, a white envelope arrives at the Majorna address. Official letters follow a fixed pattern: a heading that says what kind of letter it is (*Beslut*, a decision), the decision itself, the reason, and what you can do if you disagree.

blocks.title: Skatteverket — Beslut om folkbokföring
items: Skatteverket har beslutat att du är folkbokförd på adressen Karl Johansgatan 12, c/o Hanna Lindqvist, 414 59 Göteborg, fr.o.m. den 28 augusti.
Beslutet har fattats med anledning av din flyttanmälan.
Om du anser att beslutet är felaktigt kan du överklaga det. Information om hur du gör finns på nästa sida.
Med vänlig hälsning
Skatteverket

What it means
rows: officially registered as living at an address
as of, starting from and including
the decision has been made (s-passive of *fatta ett beslut*)

blocks.text: Abbreviations are everywhere in official Swedish, and they are always read out in full: **fr.o.m.** (från och med), **t.o.m.** (till och med), **t.ex.** (till exempel), **bl.a.** (bland annat, among other things), **s.k.** (så kallad, so-called), **enl.** (enligt, according to), **ang.** (angående, regarding).

**Personnummer** has ten digits (twelve with the century): birth date + four more. *990412-3456* is someone born on April 12, 1999. The third of the last four digits is odd for men and even for women, and the last one is a check digit. A *samordningsnummer*, for people who are not registered as residents, looks the same but adds 60 to the day: *990472-…*

head: Agency
What it does for you
rows: population register, personnummer, ID card, address changes, income tax
social insurance: sick pay, parental benefit, child allowance
healthcare advice and your local health center, based on your registered address

blocks.title: Renting second-hand: a checklist
items: A **written contract** with dates, rent, deposit and notice period. Read it through (*läsa igenom*) before you sign (*skriva under*).
Check what is **included**: *El och internet ingår* (electricity and internet included).
To see the **permission** (*tillstånd*) from the landlord or the housing association.
**Reasonable rent**: the first-hand tenant may not make a profit, only charge the rent plus a fair surcharge for furniture.
Pay by **bank transfer or Swish**, never in cash, so there is a record.
Take **photos** of the apartment on the day you move in.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 13
items: Officialese loves the passive. Rewrite these with *man* or with the agency as subject: *Beslutet har fattats* → *Skatteverket har fattat beslutet.* *Blanketten ska skickas in senast fredag* → *Man ska skicka in blanketten senast fredag.*
Then go the other way: *Arbetsgivaren drar av skatten* → *Skatten dras av.* *Man betalar ut lönen den 25:e* → *Lönen betalas ut den 25:e.*
